answer: The Mechatronics Engineering program provides a solid education for a professional career or graduate study, instilling moral and professional responsibility, self-learning and leadership, mainly in Lebanon and the Middle East; graduates apply multidisciplinary knowledge, pursue advanced study and take leadership roles.

source_quote: Upon successful completion of the BS/BE program in Mechatronics Engineering,
answer: Mechatronics graduates achieve the seven ABET-style outcomes: complex problem solving, engineering design, communication, ethical responsibility, teamwork, experimentation and data analysis, and acquiring new knowledge.

answer: The Bachelor of Engineering in Mechatronics Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria (no applicable program criteria).

answer: Mechatronics engineers work in food processing, building and construction, medical and pharmaceutical industries, aerospace, automotive, chemical, oil and gas, computers and electronics, renewable energy and more, with emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering (BE) program in Mechatronics Engineering comprises 152
answer: The BE in Mechatronics Engineering is 152 credits over eight regular and three summer semesters; the BS is 118 credits over six regular and three summer semesters. Both require a CGPA, major GPA and SLP grade of 70 or above.
BS in Mechatronics Engineering (118 credits): General Education 27 (23%), College Requirements 24 (20%), Program Requirements 67 (57%); major 28 mandatory, non-major 84 mandatory + 6 elective.

BE in Mechatronics Engineering (152 credits): General Education 30 (20%), College Requirements 27 (18%), Program Requirements 95 (62%: 80 mandatory + 15 elective); major 41 mandatory + 15 elective, non-major 87 mandatory + 9 elective.

Mechatronics mandatory courses: CCEE 221/221L, CIVE 211, ELEC 320/320L, ELEC 331, MECA 340, 341/341L, 400 (BS project; BE takes an elective), 440/440L, 441, 442, 443/443L, 444, 444L, 445, 499 Co-op, 541, 542, 544, 595A, 595B, 15 credits of MECA 4xx/5xx electives, and MECH 200, 220, 224, 320/320L, 321, 333, 421, 422.

answer: The Mechatronics SLP is 3 credits for the BS and 4 for the BE (1 credit then 3 credits in consecutive regular semesters), preferably in groups on an industry or community problem.

source_quote: Students must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their interests.
answer: Mechatronics students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (MECA 499, 3 credits), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, a formal report, poster and presentation; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.

Mechatronics Year 1 Fall (15 credits): CCEE 214, CIVE 211, ENGL 210, MATH 215, PHYS 210. Spring (15 credits): ELEC 210, MATH 216, MECH 200, MECH 220, Humanities/Fine Arts Elective I. Summer (9 credits): CHEM 211, MECH 224, MATH 311.

Mechatronics Year 2 Fall (17 credits): CCEE 221, ELEC 320/320L, MATH 314, MECH 320/320L, MECH 321. Spring (17 credits): CCEE 221L, ENGL 217, MATH 351, MECA 340, MECA 341/341L, MECH 333. Summer (9 credits): ENGR 300, MATH 317, Social Sciences/Cultural Elective I.

Mechatronics Year 3 Fall (16 credits): MECA 440, MECA 441, MECA 442, MECA 444L, MECA 541, MECH 421. Spring (17 credits): ARAB 212, ELEC 331, MATH 421, MECA 440L, MECA 443/443L, Community & Sustainability, Technical Elective I (BS project for BS). Summer (3 credits): MECA 499 Co-op; these 118 credits complete the BS.
